extracted.intended_audience: administrative law scholars, agency rulemakers, regulators, and researchers of public participation/notice-and-comment
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for evaluating and valuing lay/experiential public comments submitted during administrative notice-and-comment rulemaking, emphasizing situated knowledge and alternative vetting criteria to complement traditional legal/technical criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish regulations from statutory requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Insiders value comments that distinguish regulations from statutory requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the traditional 'insider' criteria that reward legalistic analysis; implies commenters identify whether an issue is a matter of agency rulemaking versus statutory interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrate statutory understanding through interpretive text
rubrics_metrics.description: Insiders value comments that demonstrate statutory understanding via interpretive text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reflects 'thinking like a lawyer'—showing command of statutory language and its interpretation as support for regulatory claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Propose explicit regulatory changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Insiders value comments that propose explicit regulatory changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concrete, actionable rule text or specific amendment proposals are favored by traditional evaluators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide examples or logical arguments supporting positions
rubrics_metrics.description: Insiders value comments that provide examples or logical arguments supporting positions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analytic structure (premise-argument-conclusion) and logical reasoning are hallmark features of insider-valued comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include legal, policy, or empirical background
rubrics_metrics.description: Insiders value comments that include legal, policy, or empirical background.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citation to law, policy literature, or empirical studies bolsters a comment's credibility under insider standards; these criteria reward quantitative/technical evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact information from ground-level experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Situated knowledge contribution: impact information drawn from ground-level, lived experience of the regulated activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes concrete harms, burdens, or operational realities that only on-the-ground actors typically observe; complements but differs from legal/empirical background.

rubrics_metrics.name: Knowledge of ambiguities and enforcement gaps
rubrics_metrics.description: Situated knowledge contribution: identification of ambiguities and enforcement gaps that insiders may not see.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical awareness of how rules are enforced (or not), and where regulatory language creates loopholes in real usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unintended-consequence prediction (user perspective)
rubrics_metrics.description: Situated knowledge contribution: prediction of unintended consequences from the user/participant perspective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forward-looking, grounded forecasts about downstream effects that technical/legal analysis can miss.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local contextual factors affecting rule operation
rubrics_metrics.description: Situated knowledge contribution: local contextual factors that affect how a rule will operate in practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details about place-specific, community, or operational constraints that shape real-world implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complexity accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: A type of valuable experiential comment that reveals contradictions inside seemingly unified interest groups (e.g., a small landlord whose interests differ from large landlords).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These accounts complicate simplified stakeholder categories and show intra-group variation; useful for agencies to avoid overgeneralizing from organizational positions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contributory context accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: A type of valuable experiential comment that identifies root causes outside the agency's regulatory authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows how non-regulatory factors contribute to observed problems, helping agencies understand limits of regulatory fixes and potential need for coordination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unintended-consequences accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: A type of valuable experiential comment that predicts downstream effects the agency missed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grounded predictions about policy ripple effects, informing agencies about possible negative or unexpected outcomes of a proposed rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reframing accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: A type of valuable experiential comment that surfaces overlooked competing values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offers new frames or value perspectives that shift how the problem or preferred solution is seen, prompting agencies to reconsider tradeoffs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal coherence
rubrics_metrics.description: Alternative vetting criterion: does the narrative hang together?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When statistical representativeness is impossible, assess whether the experiential account is internally consistent and plausible as a single report.

rubrics_metrics.name: External plausibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Alternative vetting criterion: is the account consistent with known facts?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-check narratives against established facts, empirical literature, or observable realities to judge plausibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repeated corroboration
rubrics_metrics.description: Alternative vetting criterion: do multiple commenters describe the same phenomenon?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for recurrence across independent submissions as a signal that a described experiential pattern is real rather than idiosyncratic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe a specific lived experience with the regulated activity
rubrics_metrics.description: Rubric checkbox: Does the commenter describe a specific lived experience with the regulated activity?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operationalizes 'situated knowledge'—specific, concrete narratives are more valuable than abstract assertions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surface contradiction, gap, or unintended consequence
rubrics_metrics.description: Rubric checkbox: Does the comment surface a contradiction, gap, or unintended consequence the agency may have missed?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek accounts that reveal problems not apparent in the agency's proposal or in traditional legal analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative cohere internally and align with known facts
rubrics_metrics.description: Rubric checkbox: Does the narrative cohere internally and align with known facts?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combines internal coherence and external plausibility vetting: the story should be consistent and not conflict with available evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduce absent value or perspective
rubrics_metrics.description: Rubric checkbox: Does the comment introduce a value or perspective absent from the proposal?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlights contributions that broaden the agency's view of affected interests, values, or impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experiential claim recurs in other comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Rubric checkbox: Does the comment's experiential claim recur in other comments (suggesting a real pattern)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages agencies to weigh repeated, similar firsthand reports as evidence of systemic issues when representative sampling is unavailable.
